The cost spike on 2025-09-22 for account tVENWJP comes from a new application, **d7I**, which first appears in the data that day.

- **Where the increase showed up:** One cloud service, l5O5g, rose from about $650–730 a day (Sept 15–21) to $1,227 on Sept 22. It then stayed around $1,170–1,280 a day through Sept 26. Every other service stayed within its normal daily range.
- **What caused it:** All of that increase comes from application d7I. It has no rows before Sept 22, cost $539 that day, and has continued at roughly $510–570 a day since. The applications that were already running under l5O5g changed by only a few dollars each.
- **What d7I consists of:** It runs on 9 instance types (instance families) that are also new on Sept 22 and used only by d7I. Each one has 7–10 instances costing $43–70 a day. Because they all belong to the new application, I report the application as the single root cause rather than listing each instance type.

Service 6K5fR also went up by about $130 that day but fell back the next day. I treated that as normal day-to-day variation, not part of the anomaly.
